findings.function: most non-getter functions (claimComp x3, borrowAllowed, redeemAllowed, transferAllowed, mintAllowed, seizeAllowed, liquidateBorrowAllowed, repayBorrowAllowed, _setCompSpeeds, exitMarket ...)
findings.issue: Error(string) reverts whose buffer starts at the free-memory pointer are not recognized: 585 'revert with memory' lines against 60 'revert with ...' strings, the selector prints as a 63-digit word (all 215 P6 lines) and the message as a hex word. Where the base is a constant (borrowAllowed 6091, 6138) the same code prints revert with 'borrow is paused'.
findings.rule: With mem[64] >= 128 established (every store to slot 64 is a constant >= 128 or itself plus a non-wrapping amount), stores at mem[64] + c do not alias slot 64, so _147 - mem[64] folds to 0; then a revert of mem[p len 100 (+32k)] holding 0x08c379a0, 32, n, the n bytes is 'revert with <string>', exactly as for constant p.

findings.function: every function using ExponentialNoError add_/sub_/mul_/div_ with an error string (211 whiles)
findings.decompiled: _94 = mem[64] / mem[64] = _94 + 96 / mem[_94 + 32] = 21 / mem[_94 + 64] = 0x737562747261...('subtraction underflow') / if _92 > _91: ... _97 = mem[_94 + 32] / idx = 32 / while idx < _97: mem[_95 + idx + 68] = mem[_94 + idx + 64]; idx = idx + 32 / ... revert with memory
findings.source: ExponentialNoError sub_(uint a, uint b, string memory errorMessage): require(b <= a, errorMessage)
findings.issue: 211 of the text's 244 whiles copy a constant error message from memory into the revert buffer. The message length was stored three lines earlier (mem[_94 + 32] = 21) but is re-read as unknown because the stores at _95 = mem[64] are not known to miss it, so the copy stays a loop and the revert stays raw memory.
findings.rule: Two addresses b + c1 and b' + c2 with b' = b + k (k a known constant, here mem[64] = _94 + 96 just stored) are disjoint when their constant offsets differ by at least the access width; fold the read of mem[_94 + 32] to 21, which makes the copy a fixed 1-word copy and the revert 'revert with 'subtraction underflow''.

findings.decompiled: while _2206 <= v: ... if y + 1 < mem[128]: _2267 = mem[32 * y + 192] else: ... s = s + 1; continue loop1 ... continue / (after the loop) mem[_2209 + 36] = mem[_2208 + 32] ... revert with memory
findings.source: Comptroller.sol:1668 for (uint j = 0; j < holders.length; j++) distributeSupplierComp(address(cToken), holders[j]); (distributeSupplierComp: sub_(supplyIndex.mantissa, supplierIndex.mantissa) )
findings.issue: The supplier loop over holders is rotated: its first iteration is printed before the loop, and the loop header is the 'subtraction underflow' test of the next iteration's sub_, whose exit leads only to the revert after the loop. The real bound j < holders.length appears inside the body as 'if y + 1 < mem[128]' with 'continue loop1' as the exit.
findings.rule: When choosing the loop condition of a structured loop, do not use a test whose exit edge reaches only a revert; print such a test as a require inside the body and take the remaining exit test (here y + 1 < mem[128]) as the while condition.

findings.issue: Shrinking the array by one deletes exactly the old last element, but prints as a storage range with a max() length.
findings.rule: x > x - 1 iff x != 0; for x = n + sha3(..) with n >= 1, max(x, x - 1) = x (keccak taken collision-free, so x != 0), the length is 1 and the store is assetsIn[caller][_353 - 1] = 0.

notes: Very long functions (claimComp variants ~1,200-1,500 lines, transferAllowed ~1,500, redeemAllowed ~1,200) reviewed by structure. Source loops (11): enterMarkets (637), exitMarket search (4038, while True with breaks), getHypotheticalAccountLiquidityInternal (1130, 2025, 2953, 3548, 5208, 6265, 10317 area), _addMarketInternal (604), _setMarketBorrowCaps (450), fixBadAccruals (731), _setCompSpeeds (4100), claimComp's 4 loops (outer 'loop1', borrower inner 'while t < mem[128]', rotated supplier inner, grant loop at the end). Implicit: 12 storage-to-memory copies of accountAssets/allMarkets printed as rotated whiles (first element before the loop), counted in P3 with the 3 rotated supplier loops; 211 error-string copies (P7). Owner paths (_setCollateralFactor, _supportMarket, _setCompSpeeds) and error codes match the source. grantCompInternal's COMP address is the hard-coded 0xfaba6f...9be3, as in the source.
summary: Faithful, but readability is dominated by the untracked free-memory pointer: 585 raw-memory reverts and 211 error-message copy loops make up most of the text, and claimComp's supplier loop is rotated around an underflow check.
